v4, written: the closer now remembers the opener. The 7/4 interlude (siete) opens with SEVEN DOORS, the head of t1 Doors at Seven, a whole step up on the rotary rhodes over the stretched clave - reharmonised as Doors at Seven's own changes in D (Dm11 / Ebmaj7#11 / A7alt) before the interlude's Bbmaj7#11 / A7sus music returns - so the album's first and last tracks share their 7/4 theme. And the final shout gets a MONA, the Afro-Cuban arranger's stacked riff: french horns low in the gaps of the mambo riff (D . F E . | . C D . note: v5, written: REAL CONGAS. The clave suite gets its hand drums: a quinto (E4), a conga (B3) and a slap built on chirper-two's physical drum layer (open-bottomed heads, a short felt contact for open tones, hard plastic with full slap for the slap), tuned and sounding at pitch. They take over from the kit's rack toms: the son/mambo tumbao now has its slap on 2 and open tones on 4 and 4&, the bembe and descarga a slap on each half-bar, and the quinto answers; the floor tom stays underneath as the low drum, and the master's low shelf rises (120 Hz +6 -> +12 dB) to give back the weight the rack toms carried. compscore seeds 0/11/19/29 (guardrail): v4 97.823/97.817/97.823/97.819 -> v5 97.941/97.938/97.942/97.935, six sections on every seed (spectrum 96.7 -> 98.0). note: v6, written: the descarga gets VOICES and a talking drum. The CORO is now sung as well as blown: a baritone on chirp's voice engine (maynard) an octave under the horns, its vowel moving a / e / o note by note, with a wordless choir (dream-vox) at pitch - the Afro-Cuban coro answering the soloists (measured solo: -19 dBFS in the coro bars, silent between). note: v7, written: THE PIANO'S TURN - a new 16-bar piano solo over the montuno groove between the son and the mambo, the Latin-jazz piano feature the suite lacked. The horns lay out; over clave, congas and the tumbao the piano's right hand plays in octaves on syncopated eighth cells (x.xx.x.x / .x.xx.xx / xx.x.xx., the fourth bar of each four repeating the first so the phrases rhyme), its lines drawn from each chord's own scale (D dorian, G mixolydian, C lydian, A altered) and its top climbing a semitone every two bars; the master dips 3 dB, so the mambo's horns land harder.
